name: gizza-ai/rabbit-cipher
summary: Encrypt or decrypt data with the Rabbit stream cipher (128-bit key, optional 64-bit IV)

tool.description: Encrypt or decrypt data with the Rabbit stream cipher (RFC 4503 / eSTREAM), a fast 128-bit-key, 64-bit-IV stream cipher. operation = encrypt (default) or decrypt — Rabbit is symmetric, so both apply the same keystream. key must resolve to exactly 16 bytes: a 16-char UTF-8 passphrase (key_format=text, default) or hex/base64 (key_format=encoded). iv is optional and, when given, must resolve to exactly 8 bytes; it must match on both sides. The ciphertext (and an encoded key/IV) use format = hex (default) or base64; the plaintext is UTF-8. Keys and IVs are read most-significant-byte first, matching the RFC 4503 test vectors.

data.description: For encrypt: the plaintext (UTF-8). For decrypt: the ciphertext, encoded with `format`.

format.description: Encoding for the ciphertext (and the key/IV when key_format=encoded): hex (default) or base64. The plaintext is always UTF-8 text.

iv.description: Optional initialization vector. Must resolve to exactly 8 bytes (64 bits) when given: 8 UTF-8 chars (key_format=text) or 16 hex chars / 12 base64 chars (key_format=encoded). Leave empty for no IV. Must match on encrypt and decrypt.

key.description: The Rabbit key. Must resolve to exactly 16 bytes (128 bits): a 16-character UTF-8 passphrase when key_format=text (default), or 32 hex chars / 24 base64 chars when key_format=encoded.

key_format.description: How to read the key and IV: text = UTF-8 bytes (default); encoded = hex/base64 per `format`.

operation.description: encrypt (default) or decrypt. Rabbit is symmetric, so both apply the same keystream.
